entries.prompt: To put right something broken, so it works again.
entries.hint: The first part means again.
entries.why: Re- means again. Repair comes from a Latin word meaning to make ready again.

entries.prompt: To put up again a thing that has fallen down.
entries.hint: The start means again; the root means to make.
entries.why: Re- (again) + build: to build a thing again after it falls.

entries.prompt: To bring two parts together once more, after they came apart.
entries.hint: Re- means again.
entries.why: Re- (again) + join: to join two parts again.

entries.prompt: To fix one thing firmly to another so it holds.
entries.hint: The root means firm; -en means to make.
entries.why: Fast (firm, fixed) + -en (to make): to make a thing firm, so it holds.

entries.prompt: To bring something back to how it was before it was harmed.
entries.hint: The first part means again.
entries.why: Re- means again: to restore is to make a thing stand as it was again.

entries.prompt: To make something like new again.
entries.hint: The root is the opposite of old.
entries.why: Re- (again) + new: to make a thing new again.

entries.prompt: To mend and equip a ship again, for another voyage.
entries.hint: Re- means again; the root means to suit.
entries.why: Re- (again) + fit: to fit a ship out again, mended and ready.

entries.prompt: To make something stronger by adding support.
entries.hint: The root means strength.
entries.why: Re- (again) + in + force (strength): to put strength back in.

entries.prompt: To make something stronger.
entries.hint: -en at the end means to make.
entries.why: Strength + -en (to make): to make a thing stronger.

entries.prompt: To fix a fallen part on once more.
entries.hint: The root means to fasten on.
entries.why: Re- (again) + attach (to fasten on): to fasten a part on again.

entries.prompt: To put the parts of something together once more, after it was taken apart.
entries.hint: The root means to gather together.
entries.why: Re- (again) + assemble (to gather together): to put the parts together again.

entries.prompt: To bring a worn machine or tool back into good working order.
entries.hint: Condition means the state a thing is in.
entries.why: Re- (again) + condition (the state of a thing): to bring a thing back into good condition.

entries.prompt: To put a new part where a worn one was.
entries.hint: The root is a spot where a thing goes.
entries.why: Re- (again) + place: to put a new part in the old one's place.

entries.prompt: To take a machine apart, check every part, and put it right.
entries.hint: Two words joined: one means above, one means to pull.
entries.why: Over + haul: to go over a machine part by part and set it right.

entries.prompt: The work of bringing something back to how it was.
entries.hint: The ending -ation makes it a thing, not an action.
entries.why: Re- (again) + stor + -ation (the act of): the act of making a thing as it was.

entries.prompt: To join two parts again so they work together.
entries.hint: Con- means together; the root means to bind.
entries.why: Re- (again) + con- (together) + nect (to bind): to bind two parts together again.

entries.prompt: To make something lighter or more full of light.
entries.hint: -en at the end means to make.
entries.why: Bright + -en (to make): to make a thing bright.

entries.prompt: To set something on fire, so it starts to burn.
entries.hint: The root ign means fire.
entries.why: Ign (fire, from the Latin ignis) + -ite: to set on fire.

entries.prompt: Small, dry sticks used to start a fire.
entries.hint: -ing ends it; the root means to set alight.
entries.why: Kindle (to set alight) + -ing: the small sticks that set a fire going.

entries.prompt: Bright with the light of the sun.
entries.hint: Two short words joined: what shines by day, and what a lamp is once it burns.
entries.why: Sun + lit: lit up by the sun.

entries.prompt: Able to catch fire and burn easily.
entries.hint: The root means flame.
entries.why: Flamm (flame) + -able (able to): able to burst into flame.

entries.prompt: Sending out bright light or warmth; shining.
entries.hint: The root radi means a ray.
entries.why: Radi (a ray) + -ant (doing): sending out rays of light or warmth.

entries.prompt: Glowing with the small flames of wax sticks at night.
entries.hint: Two words: a wax light, and what it is once it burns.
entries.why: Candle + lit: lit by candles.

entries.prompt: To light a fire again after it has gone out.
entries.hint: Re- means again; the root is an old word for setting alight.
entries.why: Re- (again) + kindle (to set alight): to set a fire burning again.

entries.prompt: To throw back light, as a mirror or still water does.
entries.hint: Re- means back; the root means to bend.
entries.why: Re- (back) + flect (to bend): to bend light back, as a mirror does.

entries.prompt: Shining softly, with a gleam like polished silver.
entries.hint: -ous means full of.
entries.why: Lustr (shine) + -ous (full of): full of soft shine.

entries.prompt: To light up a dark place so it can be seen.
entries.hint: The root lumin means light.
entries.why: Il- (in, upon) + lumin (light) + -ate (to make): to throw light upon a thing.

entries.prompt: To send out rays of light or heat in every direction.
entries.hint: The root radi means a ray, like the spokes of a wheel.
entries.why: Radi (a ray) + -ate (to make): to send out rays.

entries.prompt: So bright that it almost blinds your eyes.
entries.hint: -ing ends it.
entries.why: Dazzle + -ing: so bright it dazzles, almost blinding the eye.

entries.prompt: How much light a star or lamp gives out; its brightness.
entries.hint: -ity makes a word into a thing, as in purity.
entries.why: Lumin (light) + -osity (the quality of): how much light a thing gives.

entries.prompt: The lighting up of a place, so that it is bright.
entries.hint: The root lumin means light; -ation makes it a thing.
entries.why: Il- (upon) + lumin (light) + -ation (the act of): the act of lighting a place.

entries.prompt: Great brightness, as of a light too strong to look at.
entries.hint: -ance turns a describing word into a thing.
entries.why: Brilli (to shine) + -ance (the state of): great brightness.

entries.prompt: To make something a little bit wet.
entries.hint: -en at the end means to make.
entries.why: Moist + -en (to make): to make a thing moist.

entries.prompt: A can or pipe that scatters drops of water over a garden.
entries.hint: -er names a thing that does the action.
entries.why: Sprinkle + -er (a thing that does): a thing that sprinkles water.

entries.prompt: To make an empty trough full once more.
entries.hint: Re- means again.
entries.why: Re- (again) + fill: to fill a thing again.

entries.prompt: The bringing of water to dry fields by ditches and channels.
entries.hint: -ation makes it a thing, not an action.
entries.why: Ir- (into) + rig (to water) + -ation (the act of): the act of bringing water into the land.

entries.prompt: Small drops of water in the air or the ground.
entries.hint: -ure makes it a thing.
entries.why: Moist + -ure (a thing): the wetness in the air or the soil.

entries.prompt: A heavy fall of rain.
entries.hint: Two words: one means toward the ground, one means to tip out.
entries.why: Down + pour: rain pouring down.

entries.prompt: To spill over the edge of a container that is too full.
entries.hint: Two words: one means above, one means to run like a river.
entries.why: Over + flow: to flow over the brim.

entries.prompt: To bring water to dry fields through ditches and pipes.
entries.hint: The root rig comes from a Latin word for watering.
entries.why: Ir- (into) + rig (to water) + -ate (to make): to bring water into the land.

entries.prompt: To give water to something that needs it.
entries.hint: The root hydr means water.
entries.why: Hydr (water) + -ate (to make): to give water to a thing.

entries.prompt: Able to soak up water quickly, as a sponge is.
entries.hint: -ent means doing, so the word says what the thing does.
entries.why: Absorb (to suck in) + -ent: able to suck up water.

entries.prompt: To put something fully under water.
entries.hint: Sub- means under.
entries.why: Sub- (under) + merge (to dip): to put a thing under water.

entries.prompt: To soak something so fully it can hold no more water.
entries.hint: -ate at the end means to make.
entries.why: Satur (full) + -ate (to make): to make a thing as full of water as it can be.

entries.prompt: To dip something all the way into a liquid.
entries.hint: Im- means in; the root means to dip.
entries.why: Im- (in) + merse (to dip): to dip a thing all the way in.

entries.prompt: To flood a place with a great rush of water.
entries.hint: The root und means a wave.
entries.why: In- (upon) + und (a wave) + -ate (to make): to flood over in waves.

entries.prompt: To fill something up again, such as a water barrel.
entries.hint: The root plen means full, as in plenty.
entries.why: Re- (again) + plen (full) + -ish (to make): to make full again.

entries.prompt: To add water to dry air.
entries.hint: -ify at the end means to make.
entries.why: Humid (damp) + -ify (to make): to make the air damp.

entries.prompt: To turn a key so a shut door can be pulled wide.
entries.hint: Un- means to undo.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + lock: to undo a lock.

entries.prompt: To slide back the metal rod that holds a door shut.
entries.hint: Un- undoes what the root names.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + bolt (a sliding metal rod): to slide the bolt back.

entries.prompt: To lift the little bar that keeps a gate closed.
entries.hint: The root names a gate's catch.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + latch (a gate's catch): to lift the latch.

entries.prompt: To open out a map or a cloth that was creased flat.
entries.hint: Un- means to undo.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + fold: to undo the folds.

entries.prompt: To undo whatever holds two things firmly together.
entries.hint: Un- undoes; -en means to make; the root means firm.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + fast (firm) + -en (to make): to undo what was made firm.

entries.prompt: To break the wax that closes a letter.
entries.hint: The root names the wax that closes a letter.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + seal: to break the seal.

entries.prompt: To take the lid or cloth off something.
entries.hint: Un- means to undo.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + cover: to take the cover off.

entries.prompt: To undo the hooked catch on a cloak or a book.
entries.hint: The root names a hooked metal catch.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + clasp (a hooked catch): to undo the clasp.

entries.prompt: To clear away whatever is in the way.
entries.hint: Un- means to undo.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + block: to clear what blocks the way.

entries.prompt: To lift away the beam that holds a door shut.
entries.hint: The root names a long beam.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + bar: to take the bar off a door.

entries.prompt: To take off the covering of a parcel or a gift.
entries.hint: Un- means to undo.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + wrap: to take the wrapping off.

entries.prompt: To free threads or ropes that are knotted together.
entries.hint: Un- means to undo.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + tangle: to undo a tangle.

entries.prompt: To undo the metal fastener on a belt or strap.
entries.hint: The root names a belt's metal fastener.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + buckle: to undo a buckle.

entries.prompt: Clear, with nothing blocking the way through.
entries.hint: Struct means to build; ob- means against; un- means not.
entries.why: Un- (not) + ob- (against) + struct (built) + -ed: with nothing built against the way.

entries.prompt: To take the iron rings off someone's wrists or ankles.
entries.hint: The root names an iron ring for a prisoner.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + shackle (an iron ring): to take the shackles off.

entries.prompt: To free something from a knotted, twisted mess.
entries.hint: Dis- means apart; en- means into.
entries.why: Dis- (apart) + en- (into) + tangle: to take a thing out of a tangle.

entries.prompt: To set a plant into the ground once more, in fresh soil.
entries.hint: Re- means again.
entries.why: Re- (again) + plant: to plant a thing again.

entries.prompt: A very young plant, just up out of the soil.
entries.hint: -ling means small or young, as in duckling.
entries.why: Seed + -ling (small, young): a young plant just grown from a seed.

entries.prompt: A young tree with a thin trunk.
entries.hint: -ling means small or young.
entries.why: Sap + -ling (small, young): a young tree.

entries.prompt: To make something bigger.
entries.hint: En- means to make.
entries.why: En- (to make) + large: to make a thing larger.

entries.prompt: Bearing plenty of fruit; growing well.
entries.hint: -ful means full of.
entries.why: Fruit + -ful (full of): full of fruit.

entries.prompt: To grow larger by spreading out.
entries.hint: Ex- means out.
entries.why: Ex- (out) + pand (to spread): to spread out and grow larger.

entries.prompt: To make something longer.
entries.hint: -en at the end means to make.
entries.why: Length + -en (to make): to make a thing longer.

entries.prompt: To give a plant the food it needs to grow strong.
entries.hint: The root comes from a Latin word meaning to feed.
entries.why: Nour (to feed) + -ish (to make): to feed a thing so it grows.

entries.prompt: To add manure or compost so soil grows better crops.
entries.hint: -ize means to make.
entries.why: Fertil (fruitful) + -ize (to make): to make the soil fruitful.

entries.prompt: To make soil better, so plants can grow.
entries.hint: En- means to make.
entries.why: En- (to make) + rich: to make the soil rich.

entries.prompt: To prepare the land and tend crops as they grow.
entries.hint: The root means to till the soil.
entries.why: Cultiv (tilled) + -ate (to make): to till the land and tend what grows.

entries.prompt: To dig up a plant and set it in new ground.
entries.hint: Trans- means across.
entries.why: Trans- (across) + plant: to move a plant across to new ground.

entries.prompt: To grow back a part that was lost or cut off.
entries.hint: The root gener means to bring into being.
entries.why: Re- (again) + gener (to bring into being) + -ate: to make a part grow again.

entries.prompt: To grow strongly and do very well.
entries.hint: Its root comes from the Latin for flower.
entries.why: From the Latin florere, to flower: to grow and bloom with health.

entries.prompt: To bring life and strength back to something that has grown weak.
entries.hint: The root vital means full of life.
entries.why: Re- (again) + vital (full of life) + -ize (to make): to make full of life again.

entries.prompt: Green and full of growing plants.
entries.hint: The root verd means green.
entries.why: Verd (green) + -ant: green with growing plants.
